title: Croatians rally in Zagreb and other cities over psychiatric patient death

tea.why: Protesters rallied following the death of a 32-year-old psychiatric patient, allegedly caused by medical staff's excessive use of force.
tea.want: Demonstrators gathered to pay tribute, observe silence, and protest against the treatment of psychiatric patients.
tea.changed: Nov 14: Hundreds rallied in Zagreb, Split, Dubrovnik, and Osijek after footage emerged showing medical staff restraining a patient.

summary: Demonstrations took place in Zagreb and several other Croatian cities, including Split, Dubrovnik, and Osijek, following the death of a 32-year-old psychiatric patient named Kristian Josip Periš. Organised by a student initiative, participants gathered in a central Zagreb square to observe eight minutes of silence for the deceased. The public outrage followed the release of surveillance footage showing medical personnel tying the patient to a bed, striking his chest, pressing on his body, and covering his face with a pillow. Croatian Prime Minister Andrej Plenković described the incident as murder, while prosecutors suspect staff used excessive force and violated standards. Health Minister Irena Hrstić announced that health inspectors found irregularities and that the hospital director and board have resigned.
demands: Justice and accountability for the death of the psychiatric patient
Better treatment and standards for psychiatric patients
response: Croatian Prime Minister Andrej Plenković described the incident as murder. Health Minister Irena Hrstić stated that the health inspectorate found irregularities, while prosecutors suspect suspects used excessive force. The hospital director and board resigned, according to Lokalec.si.

updates.text: Hundreds of people gathered in Zagreb and other cities for rallies following the death of a psychiatric patient.
